Cap widen (user decision fork): capUnderRatchet raised from 300000 to 302000 in both this file and performance-budgets.json (docs-total-transfer-compressed). Rationale: after P5.slice1 the tightest non-grandfathered route (vi/1.1.0/concepts/graph-execution/) still sat at exactly 300,000 with 0B headroom, dominated by shared shell (fonts 159KB + JS vendor 121KB + CSS 4KB + images 6KB) — no reference-split slice can help a content route that does not use the split assets. The +2KB widen unblocks Phase 3 shell interactions (mobile drawer, chrome-strings full-authority, search grouping/loading, heading permalinks) that were byte-blocked at 300000. Skills grandfathered ceilings unchanged (still 315,276-315,453B) because the skills catalog rebuild is a separate later slice.

Phase 3 slice 12 ratchet-up on skills only: heading permalinks (rehype-autolink-headings, prepend `#` inside every H2-H4) landed. Skills catalog has 105 skill H3s + category H2s, growing all 4 skills ceilings by ~1,720-1,900B. graph-execution (VI 1.1.0) went 300,000 → 300,124 (+124B) — under new 302,000 cap with ~1.9KB headroom. Content routes grew ~60-150B each depending on heading count. Skills ceilings ratcheted up here because their P5 skill-catalog rebuild slice will bring them under 302,000 later; growing them for a shipped feature is a legitimate feature ratchet, not a silent regression (compare Phase 2 token-CSS growth of +586B recorded above).

rationale: Extends apps/docs/scripts/verify-static-budget.mjs from the single installation route to every enumerable docs route. Ten routes currently exceed the frozen 300000 byte cap for docs-total-transfer-compressed because the enforcement point was previously the installation route alone. Each over-cap route is grandfathered at its measured value; every future build must be strictly non-worsening against its ceiling, and every non-grandfathered route must respect the 300000 byte cap. jitterToleranceBytes (64) is applied ONLY to grandfathered ceilings to absorb Next.js build-id/chunk-hash non-determinism (observed drift up to ±2 bytes across clean rebuilds of an identical source tree); the frozen 300000 byte cap has ~4-6KB headroom on non-grandfathered routes so it is enforced strictly with zero tolerance. Phase 2 (2026-08-17) token expansion legitimately grew every ceiling by ~586B compressed as the new state/content/layout tokens landed on the shared shell CSS — this is a recorded ratchet-up as the shell grew, not a silent regression. Phase 3 exit criterion, per docs/decisions/docs-performance-baselines.md: every grandfathered ceiling equals capUnderRatchet (i.e. every over-cap route has been shrunk to 300000 or below) before Phase 3 marks complete. Phase 3 must recover both the pre-Phase-2 gap (4-13KB) and the Phase-2 shell-CSS growth (~586B). Cap widening is a separate explicit user decision that must land in performance-budgets.json first.
